en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Blairstown, Warren County, New Jersey, October 1918, Sheet 2, part 1 (main map, Main Street from Water Street to Park Street)

sheet-1.description: The northern and eastern part of Blairstown village in 1918, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left of the sheet. High Street runs along the left side, with Mountain Avenue leaving it to the west near its southern end, and East Avenue runs parallel to it in the middle of the sheet; both reach Bridge Street, which crosses the sheet near its lower edge and continues east towards the Paulins Kill. Below Bridge Street the business centre begins: Main Street, Blair Place and Douglas Street run down to Water Street at the foot of the sheet, with the Presbyterian Church and its slated spire on Main Street, a bank at Main and Water Streets, a printing office and post office on Blair Place, a livery, a garage and machine shop, a blacksmith shop, a millinery and a flour, feed and grain storehouse on Bridge Street. The rest is mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings, the Valley View House boarding house on High Street, chicken houses, an auto storage building, and the farm barns at the head of East Avenue. Dutch Lane runs north from Bridge Street on the right, and the pumping station main to Paulina follows East Avenue. Blair Lake shows at the lower left. The upper right quarter of the sheet carries the title cartouche, notes on water facilities and the fire department, a small location map of New Jersey, the legend, the key map of the three sheets and the index of specials; these are outside the georeferenced mask.
notes: Mountain Avenue is Millbrook Road in OpenStreetMap.
The curving stretch of Bridge Street between East Avenue and Blair Place is drawn as part of Bridge; today it is part of Bridge Street.
Water Street's junction with Douglas Street did not agree with the modern node (about 6 m off) and was left out of the fit.
Dutch Lane is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
Population given as 1000; water works owned by Blair Academy, system installed 1890.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. High St, East Av, Mountain Av (now Millbrook Road), Bridge, Main, Douglas, Water, Blair Pl, Dutch Lane. Upper right quarter is title, notes, key, key map and index (masked out). One part.

sheet-2-1.description: The commercial centre of Blairstown in 1918, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left. Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet from Water Street at the top to Park at the foot, lined with stores: general stores, a Masonic lodge room, an ice cream parlour, a hardware and grocery, a bakery, jewellers, a harness shop, a pool room, a furniture and undertaking store, and the Blairstown House hotel. Back or Vail Street runs parallel to the east, with stables, auto houses and a blacksmith on the lots behind the Main Street stores, and Meadow Pathway leads east from it past the fire department station towards the river. Mill Creek crosses the top of the sheet with its head race and tail race; the Messler and Shannon grist mill, owned by Blair Academy, stands at Blair Lake on the upper left, with the water works auxiliary pump house beside it. West of Main Street are the Royal Theatre, the Methodist Episcopal Church and parsonage, a music hall with school rooms, a cemetery within the Blair Academy grounds, and the curving Academy road leading to the academy; Park runs diagonally to the bottom-left, and Mechanics Hall stands below Park at the foot of the sheet. The right-hand strip beyond the heavy line (the railroad yard and lumber yard) and the inset of Paulina are separate parts of the sheet and are not covered here.
notes: Back or Vail is Vail Street in OpenStreetMap; its southern end now curves to NJ 94 instead of meeting Park.
The diagonal street lettered Park is Academy Street in OpenStreetMap; the Park at the foot of the sheet is Park Street.
Placed from three junctions only (Main Street / Water Street, Main Street / Park Street, Academy Street / Park Street), so the fit passes through them exactly.
An iron foot bridge 485 ft long is noted at the heavy line; the strip beyond is drawn displaced.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north to the left. Three parts: (1) Main Street from Water to Park, Back or Vail (Vail Street), Park (Academy Street) and Park (Park Street), Mill Creek, grist mill; (2) strip beyond the heavy diagonal line: N.Y.S.&W. R.R. depot, W.C. Howell coal and lumber yard, Empire State Dairy, drawn displaced (485 ft foot bridge drawn about 150 ft); (3) inset of Paulina, 1 mile east: electric light station and water works pump house.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip east of the heavy line: N.Y.S.&W. R.R. depot, coal and lumber yard, Empire State Dairy (no street junction; the railroad (now Paulinskill Valley Trail) fixes only the cross-track position and rotation, the along-track offset of the displaced strip is unknown; needs one along-track point: the depot or a building that survives, or the Bridge Street crossing at the top of the strip, matched on modern data).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Paulina, electric light station and water works pump house, 1 mile east (outside the reference box; only country roads (to Marksboro, Hope, Blairstown), no junction checked; needs reference data around Paulina and an identified road junction or the dam).
